review: The hymn is Romans 14:17 on the kingdom: 1:1–3 is Phil 4:7 with John 14:27, 2:1–4 is Rom 14:17 (צֶדֶק וְשָׁלוֹם וְשִׂמְחָה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ) with Dan 7:14, 3:1–4 is John 14:27 with Ps 85:9, 4:1–4 is Col 1:20 with Isa 48:18, 5:1–4 is Eph 3:19 (עַל כָּל־יְדִיעָה) with Ps 4:8, and 6:1–4 is Ps 42:8 with Ps 40:3.

The shape is 3/4/4/4/4/4: stanza 1 is a three-line acclamation ending in the triple שָׁלוֹם, and the rest are four-line stanzas. The triple refrain is kept because the printed تَسْلَامٌ سَلَامٌ سَلَامٌ كُلَّ حِين sets the word three times and the repetition is the stanza.

2:2 אָפְנֵי מַלְכוּת אֵל — the Arabic أَوْصَافُ مُلْكِ الْبَارِي is 'the traits of the Creator's reign'; biblical Hebrew has no noun for 'characteristic', so the line uses אֹפֶן, the later noun for a mode or aspect, because the stanza is naming the marks by which the kingdom is recognised and not its attributes in the metaphysical sense.

3:2 הַשָּׁלוֹם הַנִּשְׂגָּב — the Arabic هٰذَا السَّلَامَ الْأَسْمَى is 'this most high peace'; the Hebrew uses the Niphal participle of שָׂגַב, the word of Isa 2:11 for what is exalted above, so the peace is above the world's reach and not merely the best of its kind.

4:3 כַּנָּהָר יָרוּץ זַךְ — the Arabic كَالنَّهْرِ يَجْرِي فِي صَفَاه is 'like a river running in its clarity'; the Hebrew compresses the prepositional phrase into the adjective זַךְ, the word of Song 5:12 and Hab 3:9 for pure water, because the line has to end on the river's purity and the stanza's next line is about drinking.
